title: Microburst sampling and dashboard approximation proposal
body:
Context:
We keep hitting two related pain points during bursty traffic patterns (short-lived microbursts): (1) trace sampling and retention costs spike because we capture full spans for many short sessions, and (2) dashboards become noisy and slow as panels try to compute high-cardinality joins for every 1s bucket. The goal of this proposal is to outline a lightweight, staged approach for reducing cost and dashboard query pressure while preserving investigatability for real incidents.

Scope and goals:
- Primary goal: hold monthly trace+dashboard operating cost for microburst traffic within a defined budget without materially increasing time-to-root-cause for high-severity incidents.
- Secondary goal: preserve the ability to reconstruct representative sessions for at least 95% of SLO-impacting events.
- Non-goals: we are not changing sampling for long-running sessions or batch workloads in this RFC.

Key ideas (summary):
1) Event-class aware sampling: use a cheap pre-filter (request metadata + light heuristic) to tag requests as likely-microburst vs normal. For likely-microburst, apply aggressive trace sampling but keep a small fraction (1–2%) of full spans for statistical fidelity.
2) Probabilistic sketching for dashboards: replace certain heavy panels with pre-aggregated sketches (count-min, t-digest) or pre-bucketed rollups at higher cardinalities to avoid per-request joins in 1s windows.
3) Tiered trace retention on microburst tag: short full-span retention (7d) and extended lightweight-provenance retention (30d) storing only headers/trace-id + minimal annotations for sampled microburst traces.
4) Synthetic probe augmentation: where sampling drops real traces, fill gaps with targeted synthetic probes (session replay style) triggered heuristically after a spike to validate system-level failure modes.

Design details:
Pre-filter heuristic and tagging:
- Input signals: request_size, route_type (embed/generate/chat), tenant_tier, token_count_estimate, short_connection_duration (<500ms), error_flag (4xx/5xx), qps-momentum (delta over 10s).
- Lightweight classifier: a ruleset executed by ingestion edge (or first hop) that sets observability.tag = microburst-likely if (short_connection_duration && token_count_estimate < 80 && qps-momentum > 3x baseline) OR (route_type=="banner" && tenant_tier=="free" && qps-momentum > 5x).
- Recorded as a boolean tag on metrics/trace headers for downstream sampling decisions.

Sampling policy:
- For requests WITHOUT microburst-likely: keep baseline sampling (1% full traces, 10% spans for session reconstruction) — unchanged.
- For microburst-likely requests: 0.5% full traces (capture spans & payloads), 5% lightweight traces (headers + span ids + status codes), and probabilistic event counters for sampled tokens.
- Emergency override: if SLI breach detected (e.g., tail latency > threshold OR error rate > threshold), temporarily escalate microburst sampling to 5% full traces for 5 minutes then decay.

Trace retention tiers and storage sketch:
- Full trace objects: store for 7d for microburst-likely; cost accounted to "microburst-burst" bucket.
- Lightweight trace metadata rows: store trace-id, route, tenant, error flags, latency quantiles, and sketch references for 30d.
- Archive policy: after 30d compress and downsample to monthly aggregates (counts by tenant/route/error-bin).

Dashboard approximation strategies:
- Identify panels to replace with approximations: high-cardinality latency heatmaps, per-tenant cold-cache rates, and kv-eviction correlation joins.
- Techniques per panel: use t-digest for p50/p95/p99 latencies; count-min for heavy hitters (top tenants/routes); pre-aggregated bucketed counters for 1s windows (roll up to 5s when microburst tag present).
- UI affordance: annotate panels with a small badge when they are in "approximation mode" (e.g., orange dot) and allow quick toggles to request higher fidelity (which will temporarily raise sampling for that filter).

Experiment matrix (quick A/B plan):
- Phase A (2 weeks): Enable pre-filter tagging and shadow-sampling (no change to retention). Measure classifier precision/recall against manual labeling from prior incidents. Metrics: fraction flagged, cost delta in trace ingestion, number of high-severity incidents with no full traces.
- Phase B (3 weeks): Enable sampling policy changes in a canary region (eu-west-1). Run dashboards on sketch backends for a subset of teams. Metrics: dashboard query latency, panel error vs baseline, operator time-to-root-cause on controlled drills.
- Phase C (4 weeks): Roll retention tiers and UI toggles; enable emergency override logic. Track cost, SLI regressions, oncall playbook activations.

Validation & failure modes:
- Risk: classifier false negatives (microburst requests not tagged) -> we keep baseline sampling so risk is low.
- Risk: classifier false positives -> additional sample reduction for normal traffic could reduce fidelity; mitigate by setting conservative thresholds in Phase A and monitoring manual label mismatch.
- Risk: operators miss that panels are approximated -> mitigate by panel badges and weekly ops training + dashboard runbook updates.

Operational playbook notes:
- Oncall steps for a detected SLI spike:
  1) Check "microburst-likely" metric spike dashboard. If present, enable emergency override (button) to increase sampling for the next 5 minutes.
  2) Trigger synthetic probe suite for affected route (automated in runbook) to capture deterministic signals.
  3) If deeper dive needed, use UI toggle on the impacted dashboard to request temporary high-fidelity traces; this schedules a short-term sampling lift.

Metrics to collect during rollout:
- classifier_precision, classifier_recall (daily), microburst_flag_rate, full_trace_ingest_bytes_by_bucket, dashboard_query_p95_by_panel, operator_ttr_median_for_incidents_with_microburst, synthetic_probe_success_rate, cost_delta_percent_observability_bucket.

Action items & owners:
- implement pre-filter rules in edge (DEADLINE: 2025-11-20) -> owner: Marcus Li -> JIRA-OP-1234
- build lightweight-trace schema + retention job -> owner: Priya Shah -> JIRA-OP-1241
- dashboard sketch backend proofs (t-digest/count-min) -> owner: Diego Fernandez -> GH PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-tooling/pull/418
- ops UI badge + sampling toggle -> owner: Aisha Patel -> JIRA-UI-88
- run Phase A labeling exercises -> owner: Observability interns (bootcamp) -> task: CONFLUENCE-OBS-2345

Notes-to-self / loose ends:
- Need SLO for how long operators tolerate approximations before forced fidelity (propose 72 hours max) — discuss in next sync.
- Evaluate whether synthetic probes should be tenant-scoped (privacy) or global (cheaper).
- Check with privacy/compliance about storing minimal headers for 30d (PII review).

References and related docs:
- see: rollout-readiness-mini-kit-metrics-and-trace-checklist.json for generic rollout steps (related)
- see: telemetry-sampling-budget-calculator-and-tradeoffs-playbook.json for sampling math notes.

Meeting notes (2025-11-05 quick sync):
- Diego: prototyping t-digest plugin for sketch backend, running latency diff tests now.
- Marcus: edge tagging doable but need low CPU budget; will optimize ruleset into a compact eBPF style filter.
- Priya: retention job will live as lifecycle lambda; need cost estimate for extra 30d metadata rows.

Feedback requested from: SRE leads, oncall rotation, product-hosted-api owners (to understand signal surfaces affected).
